f4070107-bd84-5299-8132-72ae7c8a76e8.name: *Portrait of Felice Zacchia Rondanini*
f4070107-bd84-5299-8132-72ae7c8a76e8.description:
Domenico Guidi, nephew of the sculptor Giuliano Finelli, with whom he worked in Naples (1639–49), moved to the workshops of Algardi in Rome in 1649. He stayed there until the death of his master, from whom he learned the classicism that is a fundamental part of his style, although he was not as skilled in its execution.  
The bust was acquired by the Italian state from an antique market in 1907. It was initially attributed to the Berninian school on account of the elliptical shape enclosing the female figure and the “unfinished” back, a trait peculiar to Bernini on unseen surfaces. It was later attributed to 17th- and 18th-century sculptors (such as Bracci on account of the stylistic analogies with the sculptor's bust of Clement XII in the Borghese collection). It was finally attributed to Guidi, who was summoned by Bernini in 1668 to decorate the Ponte Sant'Angelo, although his style was more classical and less elaborate in form.  
The woman is probably Felice Zacchia Rondanini, daughter of Laudivio Zacchia who, once widowed, gave his life to religion and was made a cardinal in 1626. Algardi made a portrait of the father, having already made several busts for the Rondanini family. For his part, Guidi was responsible for the Rondanini tomb in S. Maria del Popolo, Rome in 1657. In 1683, in the same church, he sculpted the funerary monument to Vincenza Danesi, who some scholars connect to the Borghese portrait, although there is no documentation to support the theory. A ring is fixed under the cloak, which suggests it was originally intended to be placed in a niche, and the measurements coincide with the anchor points of the Danesi monument.  
The old lady wears a large veil forming a convex shape, on which shadows accentuate the face in the foreground, which is struck by light. The detail on the face is particularly interesting, especially the deep lines on the face and neck and the wart on the right cheek, emphasising the realism of the portrait.  
Guidi was so well regarded by the French for his classicism that by the end of his career he was a synonym for French taste. Nonetheless, a sculptural group made for Louis XIV failed to please the king and it ended up in the same place as Bernini's: the gardens of Versailles.
f4070107-bd84-5299-8132-72ae7c8a76e8.short_description:
A portrait of an old lady who wears a veil. The detail on the face is particularly interesting, especially the deep lines on the face and neck and the wart on the right cheek, emphasising the realism of the portrait.  
Guidi produced a few works for Bernini (such as the *Angel with a Lance* on Ponte Sant'Angelo) most of his collaborative work was, however, with Algardi.

f5ef250e-6f10-578b-9290-9c8967a2f518.name: *Conversion of St. Paul* Altarpiece
f5ef250e-6f10-578b-9290-9c8967a2f518.description:
A Rococo type of *reredos* (retable) with ornamental pilasters instead of columns, and a wealth of Rococo ornamentation in compact form. At the centre is the *Conversion of St. Paul*, flanked by two female saints without attributes. Two angels kneel at the corners of the cornice. The central, upper section of the altarpiece holds the coat of arms of the Halper-Sigetski family.  
Initially, the altarpiece stood in St. Mark's Church in Zagreb, near the triumphal arch. Like most altarpieces in the church, this one was commissioned by a particular guild, the boot-makers' guild. Its production was part funded by a donation from Anna Gerlichich in 1760, as an inscription on the altarpiece details.  
The altarpiece is by an accomplished master, showing a high level of design and technical skill. The influence of Vid Königer (one of the greatest Styrian sculptors of the second half of the 18th century) is apparent, seen in the female saints in particular.  
During restoration of St Mark's at the end of the 19th century, the altarpiece was moved to the chapel of Zajezda Manor in Hrvatsko zagorje, at that time owned by Baron Halper-Sigetski, who placed his baronial arms on it.
f5ef250e-6f10-578b-9290-9c8967a2f518.short_description:
A richly carved Rococo altarpiece: two saints stand either side of twisted pilasters and two angels decorate the attic, while the central scene of the *Conversion of St Paul* is in high relief.  
Commissioned for St Mark's Church by the boot-makers' guild in 1760, it was part-funded by a donation from Anna Gerlichich, as an inscription on the altarpiece details.  
During restoration of the church at the end of the 19th century, the altarpiece was moved to the chapel of Zajezda Manor in Hrvatsko zagorje, at that time owned by Baron Halper-Sigetski, who placed his baronial arms on it.
f5ef250e-6f10-578b-9290-9c8967a2f518.dimensions: H: 226 cm; w: 258 cm; depth 70 cm
f5ef250e-6f10-578b-9290-9c8967a2f518.method_for_datation:
By stylistic analysis and research.  
During restoration and conservation work an older painted layer was discovered under the coat of arms revealing letters next to the frame and the year: "S. D. M. ANNA SAN(C) NATA DE GERLICHISCH 1760". Anna Gerličić, whose name appears on the coat of arms, probably sponsored some of the work for this altarpiece, such as the gilding.
f5ef250e-6f10-578b-9290-9c8967a2f518.provenance: Boot-Makers’ Guild altarpiece, Church of St. Mark, Zagreb
f5ef250e-6f10-578b-9290-9c8967a2f518.obtention: During restoration of St. Mark’s Church by architects Schmidt and Bollé (1876–1882), in 1880, the altarpiece was moved to the chapel of the former Patačić Manor in Zajezda. It is probable that the coat of arms of the Halper-Sigetski family was applied to the altarpiece while at Zajezda Manor in Hrvatsko zagorje, from where it was transferred to Zagreb.

f811818c-63f6-5385-94c0-2eb1a870aecb.name: Chapel of the Rosary, basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
f811818c-63f6-5385-94c0-2eb1a870aecb.description: The complex painted decoration of Mitelli and Colonna involves four pilasters, two archivolts, the walls and the vaults of the whole chapel. The painters were helped by the sculptor Domenico Ottani, who made the stucco decorations, the capitals and the elegant friezes, and the gilders Alessandro Miselli and Carlo Veronese. The abundant use of gold leaf for the decorations gives the chapel its typical baroque sumptuousness and contributes to the diffusion of light. Mitelli and Colonna started working in February 1655, completing the painting in May 1657. The subject chosen was the glorification of the Blessed Virgin of the Rosary. The dome is decorated with a beautiful sky wherein the Madonna is carried up by the angels and crowned. In the roundels at the base of the dome are represented the merits of the Rosary handed by the Virgin to St. Dominic in order to defeat the plague of 1630. Putti, angels and Virtues celebrate the glory of the Virgin among flowers, in one of the most impressive scenes of Emilian baroque. The altar is framed by illusionistic architecture on the apse and crowned by two choirs of angels holding crowns, one of flowers and one of stars thus following the motto “*Dat flores tellus, coelum dat sidera sertis*”. Three great ovals frame episodes from the life of the Virgin (the *Birth of Mary*, *Mary presented to the temple* and the *Marriage of the Virgin*). This extraordinary fresco decoration ideally faces the *Glorification of St. Dominic* painted by Guido Reni in the chapel dedicated to the saint, just across the nave.
f811818c-63f6-5385-94c0-2eb1a870aecb.short_description:
The Chapel of the Rosary was created in 1589 when the Brotherhood of the Rosary refurbished the medieval chapel held by the Guidotti family.  
Particularly striking is the altar framing the statue of the Madonna of the Rosary, surrounded by 15 small pictures with the mysteries of the Rosary, work of many celebrated Bolognese painters.  
In the second half of the seventeenth-century the interior of the chapel was rebuilt with a new dome and a new apse, while the exterior held the polygonal late Gothic features. Between 1655 and 1657 the whole chapel was decorated by the painters Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli, who made the present rich scenographic decoration, glorifying the Blessed Virgin of the Rosary.

f811818c-63f6-5385-94c0-2eb1a870aecb.history: In 1460 Giovanni Guidotti asked the mason Giovanni del Lago di Como to build a chapel in the church of San Domenico imitating that dedicated to St. Thomas, in Gothic style. The chapel was named the Guidotti chapel. In 1575, with the Guidotti's permission, the confraternity of the Rosary started to use the chapel for its meetings and in 1589 paid for its total refurbishment. Among the most significant works of art of this period stand the sumptuous altar dedicated to the Virgin and the decoration of the vault. In 1601 the most celebrated workshops in Bologna commissioned 15 paintings that now surround the statue of the Virgin and represent the Mysteries of the Rosary. They are representative of Bolognese contemporary painting style. After the plague of 1630 the Madonna of the Rosary became the focus of a rejuvenated religious zeal. Many gifts were presented to the chapel from the people who had survived the epidemic. In 1654 the master Francesco Dotti and the architect Francesco Martini modified the whole structure by building a deep apse and a square antechamber with a decorated vault and a dome. The painters Mitelli and Colonna were asked to decorate the chapel; they finished the work in 1657. During Dotti's refurbishing of the whole church (1727–1737) the chapel was partially changed, mainly in the liturgical apparel.

f88a365b-0b19-5fa2-8be0-31a30d035b7c.name: Breakfast Set
f88a365b-0b19-5fa2-8be0-31a30d035b7c.description: The breakfast set consists of a triangular tray, a sugar bowl, teapot, milk jug, high and low cups with saucers and porcelain teaspoons. The tray has rounded corners and a bevelled, scalloped rim. The teapot is potbellied with a curving handle and a tubular spout. The milk jug has a potbellied body on three short legs imitating twigs, a curved handle and short lip. The cups and the sugar bowl are simple in shape, on a low round base, and without handles. All parts of the set have gilt, lacy decorative edges. The knobs of the lids are in the shape of a rose. Each item of the set depicts a different war scene whose actors are Croatian border troops and the Pandurs of Baron Franjo Trenk, shown at moments of rest and while in action. Some of the scenes on the pieces are after Martin Engelbrecht’s prints. All items show the mark of the Meissen manufactory: crossed swords and a star, or a dot below and the impressed mark: X, P, 60, 64.
f88a365b-0b19-5fa2-8be0-31a30d035b7c.short_description: Adorning each item of the breakfast set are polychrome painted scenes of warfare with the soldiers of the Croatian border troops and the Pandurs of Baron Franjo Trenk.

ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.name: *Navis nundinaria* (The trading ship)
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.alternate_name: A ship-shaped theatre for the roast pork feast of 1657
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.description:
The *Insignia degli Anziani Consoli*, bound in 16 volumes and housed in the Archivio di Stato Bologna, are documents on parchment. They were made every two months, from 1530 to 1796, to celebrate the eight Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere di Giustizia, a group of magistrates ruling the city. From the end of the sixteenth-century, the names of the magistrates were depicted flanked by their coats of arms and a significant event that had taken place during the two months of their charge: an extraordinary visual chronicle illustrating more than two centuries of the city's history with six pictures a year.  
This picture (IV bimester of 1657) shows the stage for the roast pork feast. Celebrated every year on the 24th of August, a special installation was ssembled on the main square to host the feast of St. Bartholomew. In 1657 the theatre was shaped as a ship and was occupying nearly all the square, between the palace of the Podestà on the left and the stairs of the basilica of St. Petronius on the right. Along the sides of the ship were the stalls for the feast of the Assumption (from 15th to 24th August) that were going to become on the 24th boxes for the paying audience watching a theatrical representation and taking part in the traditional distribution of roast pork. On the mast waves the flag of the Municipality, under it a standard shows the coats of arms of Pope Alexander VII among those of the cardinal legate and of the archbishop of Bologna. On the aft deck a tent hosts the nine coats of arms of the Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere of the bimester July-August 1657. On top right a Latin inscription in golden ink describes the picture and bears the names of the Anziani Consoli.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.short_description: This illumination represents a theatre in the shape of a ship that was built on the Main Square of Bologna for the feast of the roast pork in August 1657. This was an event that attracted a great number of people every year. The ship sails are the coats of arms of the nine families of the Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere, who ruled Bologna in the bi-mester July-August 1657. On the left side of the ship, is the portico of the Palazzo del Podesta. In the background is the Pavaglione and the Palazzo dei Banchi.  The stairs on the right lead to the church of San Petronio.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.initial_owner: The Anziani Consoli of the town of Bologna
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.method_for_datation: The date and the names of the magistrates are inscribed on the top right of the picture.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.obtention: This illumination, like the whole series, has always been housed in the archive of the Bolognese senate, inside the municipal palace. It was transferred to the Archivio di Stato in 1874, when it was created.

02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.name: *St. Jacob before God as intercessor for Innsbruck, Tyrol, the Diocese of Brixen and Austria*
02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.description: The fresco cycle from Cosmas Damian Asam has the work of the church’s patron saint as its theme. Asam painted illusionistic architecture in the shallow cupolas, a task which he solved differently in each scene. There are no references to real built architecture. In the centre of the perspectively exaggerated depiction a statue of the apostle can be seen. Supplicants from all estates are gathered around him, while Jacob implores God for heavenly assistance.
02670817-41d7-5797-a20d-2808406b0faa.artist: Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739); Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750)

02c7cd31-a334-540d-862c-127ba23ad756.name: Triumphal Arch – detail
02c7cd31-a334-540d-862c-127ba23ad756.description: Basic shapes of the monument refer to Early Baroque architecture with elements of late Renaissance Classicism.

078016a8-8f27-5a98-ac04-aec12f841ef0.name: The Four Last Things
078016a8-8f27-5a98-ac04-aec12f841ef0.description: Due to John of Nepomuk’s role as the patron saint of the sacrament of confession, the significance of penance is emphasized most notably by a grouping of four confessionals in the vestibule. Their dramatic array of sculptural depictions, being rich in gesture, pertain to the “Four Last Things”: death, judgement, Heaven and Hell. These are represented by the saints Bruno, Hieronymus and Peter, as well as by a beatified believer.
078016a8-8f27-5a98-ac04-aec12f841ef0.location: The partition wall between the vestibule and the nave, both sides above the confessionals.

0791adf8-6e5c-552e-86d8-28d9c5549585.name: Welcoming figure
0791adf8-6e5c-552e-86d8-28d9c5549585.description: Glazed cobalt-blue on white *azulejos* of a welcoming figure. The character wears typical early 18th-century livery, is unarmed, and adopts a reverential attitude, his hat in hand. It is likely that the figure represents a doorkeeper in the service of the Brotherhood.
0791adf8-6e5c-552e-86d8-28d9c5549585.location: Entrance patio at the top of the staircase
0791adf8-6e5c-552e-86d8-28d9c5549585.artist: Architect unknown. Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]

0825097f-68cb-59cd-ad8a-060bcff7b3b5.name: Loggia and arcades
0825097f-68cb-59cd-ad8a-060bcff7b3b5.description: A scenographic view of the loggia shows different points of view obtained through the use of columns, balustrades and arcades. This is typical of the local baroque tradition.

090e6d2b-c30e-5e24-add9-f351134c4094.description: A vase with roses, irises and carnations.

091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.name: St. Paulo Obelisk Fountain
091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.description: From the Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras, a secondary aqueduct spreads out around the city terminating in fountains, many of them like this one still extant. Designed by Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos in 1774, it was not built until 1848, with minor adaptations by Malaquias Ferreira Leal.
091b9985-830d-5a24-aeb3-8b6403f919cf.artist: Design: Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.]; adapted by Malaquias Ferreira Leal (1790–1855)

092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.name: *Allegory of Fortune, of Love and of the Four Seasons*
092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.description: Charged by Marc’Antonio Ranuzzi, Marc’Antonio Franceschini and the quadratura painter Enrico Haffner realized the allegorical figures in the ceiling of this room on the first floor of the palace, presumably between 1680 and 1681. Very interesting and original is the allegory in the centre of the vault showing Fortune and her wheel which, moved by the wind, holds Cupid in chains.
092d3c2e-305d-5a72-89a2-85afc05e6e72.location: Ceiling decoration of a room of the first floor of the palace, Palazzo Ranuzzi

0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.name: Stucco ceiling
0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.description: The stucco ceiling, presumably also from Gigl, displays slightly different motifs and ornamentation compared to the façades. The border area is composed of intricately intertwined bands with acanthus leaves; in the centre, framed by strap and vine scroll decoration, is a star composed of bands, leaves and shells. Above the entrance to the bay window the coat of arms of the Fischer family.
0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.location: Corner room on the third floor (living quarters)

0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.name: Chapel of the Sorrowful Mother (Fieger Chapel)
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.description: Built as an extension to the vestibule, it was donated Johann Karl Graf Fieger. Together with the magnificent column altar, the most significant feature is the ceiling frescos from Kaspar Waldmann, a glorification of Mary with the seven founders of the Servite Order and scenes from the life of Mary.
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.location: Northern vestibule, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

1288aecf-a814-535b-a170-246be71bef2c.name: Painted ceiling and Small Chapel
1288aecf-a814-535b-a170-246be71bef2c.description:
In the first room is a painted wooden ceiling decorated with floral motifs. In the centre, a Portuguese Vessel (Nau) invokes St. Elmo, the patron saint of the Brotherhood.  
The second tempera painted ceiling is in the chapel. The Chapel is completely covered with gold-leaf carving in the “National” style, enhancing the shrines embedded in the walls, and exemplifying space management during the Baroque period. The ceiling depicts scenes from the Life of Saint Elmo.
1288aecf-a814-535b-a170-246be71bef2c.location: Interior rooms, House of the Holy Body (Museum of Baroque)

13b79634-03b0-538a-9826-541612b5cfbc.name: Main Altar
13b79634-03b0-538a-9826-541612b5cfbc.description: The gilded wooden altarpiece in the National style of the Portuguese Baroque.

147bc5f0-6d4a-5622-9f01-e30b4195cabf.name: Ceiling frescos
147bc5f0-6d4a-5622-9f01-e30b4195cabf.description: The central panel in the choir vault with its stucco frame depicts the Holy Family as patron saint of the brotherhood: Mary and Joseph in adoration of the Holy Trinity. Putti present carpenter’s tools as attribute and symbol of the guild. The monochrome spandrel pictures depict Joseph’s Dream, the Flight to Egypt, the Rest on the Flight and the Infant Jesus in the Workshop. On the basis of an analysis of the painting style they are variously ascribed to Paul Zeiller from Reutte or Johann Heel from Pfronten.
147bc5f0-6d4a-5622-9f01-e30b4195cabf.location: Choir, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.name: Library Façade
14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.description: Magnificent Baroque façade in limestone with four huge columns crowned by the royal coat of arms and the phrase “So highly are books praised here in Coimbra that a library crowns the city head”.

1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.name: Large reading tables
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.description: The six large tables (buffets) in multi-coloured and exotic woods are all slightly different and designed to match each room.
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.name: Monumental staircase
1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.description: For this double flight staircase Pietro Canali was inspired by theatrical stage effects. Allegorical statues of *Hercules* and *Atlas* by Gabriele Brunelli (1615–1682) decorate the staircase. The vault was painted by Gioacchino Pizzoli (1651–1731).
1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.artist: Pietro Canali; Gabriele Brunelli; Gioacchino Pizzoli

1ccb99e8-d9b9-5a4f-913c-efa249650f37.name: *Grotesco* ceiling painting
1ccb99e8-d9b9-5a4f-913c-efa249650f37.description: *Grotesco* ceiling painting with cartouches over the High Choir depicting the *Holy Trinity*, *Assumption of Our Lady* and *Escape into Egypt.*

1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.name: *Allegory of Time*
1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.description: A superb example of “quadratura” by the celebrated Angelo Michele Colonna, a specialist in painted architectures. Giuseppe Alboresi painted the figures inside the large oval at the centre of the ceiling. The scene represents the *Allegory of Time driving away Venus and the Graces*.
1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna (1604–1687) and Giuseppe Alboresi (1632–1677)

1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.name: Monumental staircase
1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.description: The monumental staircase has a complex structure, based on an elliptical plan. Two large flights of stairs embrace, rising, the area where the stair is placed; one more flight rises in the opposite direction driving to the first floor. From the balconies all around it is possible to observe the very suggestive and dynamic development of the stair, where reality and fiction are mixed up thanks to the illusive use of paintings by Ercole Graziani. Many years later Filippo Balugani realized the sculptures representing pagan gods that are placed over the balustrades.
1e1c41cd-e203-5847-9534-cb31a2f69f12.artist: Giovanni Battista Torri; Carlo Fontana; Ercole Graziani; Filippo Balugani

1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.name: Façade
1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.description: The double-tower façade of St. Jacob is a Late Baroque interpretation of a basic plan based on the Salzburg Dome. The projecting towers – which form a unit with the two-storey middle section – are characteristic. In contrast to Salzburg the transitions are more fluent, employing concave wall sections. The vertical oval windows of the upper storeys establish a number of thematic accents. The towers’ upper storeys are also more powerfully built than in Salzburg.
1f6a275f-c79d-5523-8152-e66ee749a6b7.artist: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1648–1717); Johann Georg Fischer (1673–1747)

25ede1f2-8f70-5252-9d21-3b21a63183bf.name: The Apostle Peter
25ede1f2-8f70-5252-9d21-3b21a63183bf.description: The bust, in relief of the Apostle Peter, opens onto the entrance of the chapel with six reliefs – originally gilded – of Old Testament scenes featuring motifs of sacrifice and thanksgiving by the same sculptor. Sattler also collaborated with V. Render on the Olomouc fountains.

2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.name: *The Coronation of the Virgin*
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.description: Above the frieze decorated with many golden stuccoes opens the dome, decorated with semi columns and rosettes. The open sky frames the Virgin as she is lifted to heaven to be crowned by the angels. The complex spatial articulation along with the violently vertical scene and the rapid succession of grounds achieves perfect foreshortening, a good example of the high level of Mitelli and Colonna’s achievements in decorative painting. The two painters are perfectly at ease working together so it is practically impossible to tell the different hands.
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.location: Dome of the square antechamber of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
2dabfc2d-d0c7-5629-b60d-d85fe2d540f8.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

2e812fa6-2d65-5e3f-9d13-bcf1bf2111af.name: Country house
2e812fa6-2d65-5e3f-9d13-bcf1bf2111af.description: The picturesque undulating effects of volute gables and ledges also appeared far beyond the main square, on country houses and farmhouses.

3056a9a2-f0a3-5c02-bb5f-90e9ed6e1a41.name: Organ in the High Choir
3056a9a2-f0a3-5c02-bb5f-90e9ed6e1a41.description: In the High Choir there is an Iberian organ with two symmetrical parts: the organ itself on the Epistle side and the organ pipes on the Gospel side. Friar Manuel Lourenço da Conceição from Oporto might have recycled some parts from a pre-existing organ, and Manuel Pinto de Vila Lobos designed the case.
3056a9a2-f0a3-5c02-bb5f-90e9ed6e1a41.artist:
Organ: Frei Manuel Lourenço da Conceição \[n.d.\]  
Organ cases: Manuel Pinto de Vila Lobos \[n.d.\]

33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.name: Mausoleum for Archduke Maximilian III, the German Master
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.description: The bronze mausoleum, part of the inventory of the previous building, was designed by Hubert Gerhart from Munich and was completed by Caspar Gras of Innsbruck. It is one of the most important early Baroque mausoleums, with lifelike expressiveness, above all in the depiction of the Archduke who was Grand Master of the German Order of Knights, and St. George, the order’s patron saint. The superstructure is formed of four spiral columns ranked with vines, populated by all manner of animals.
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.location: Left transept apse, St. Jacob’s Cathedral
33bda0f2-7ee5-5ec5-a93c-d5ad872cb9d3.artist: Hubert Gerhard (c. 1545–1623); Caspar Gras (1585–1674); Heinrich Reinhart (1575–1629)

37077acc-2bd2-556b-ada4-0cdd3f56fffb.name: Rua das Amoreiras Arch
37077acc-2bd2-556b-ada4-0cdd3f56fffb.description: Thanks to the architectural risk-taking of Carlos Mardel, the Rua das Amoreiras arch was built between 1746 and 1748. Two things make this monumental structure particularly notable: its innovation, for over the final perpendicular branch of the aqueduct the water galleries from Alcântara run and this had never before been seen; and the engineering – from here the aqueduct turns sharp right to the Mãe d'Água reservoir. The Amoreiras Arch frames the Rua das Amoreiras and represented at one time an “entrance”, as if it were an arch in a defensive wall, highlighting both the exceptional status of this hydraulic masterpiece and its setting.

3c569a1e-c412-5ccf-b034-acfc029ba2ad.name: Interior
3c569a1e-c412-5ccf-b034-acfc029ba2ad.description: The simple sequence of the nave and choir rectangle is accentuated and given life by slanted corners. The powerfully built arcade-above-pilaster piers between nave and choir provide a perspectival frame for the ostentatious high altar. The extremely small frescos do not form a “heaven of the saints” being restricted to delimited areas. The remaining surfaces are neither filled with frescos or stucco. While the Holy Family is depicted in the choir the pictures in the nave feature scenes of the Resurrection of Jesus, distinguished in rank by the monochrome and polychrome execution.
3c569a1e-c412-5ccf-b034-acfc029ba2ad.location: View towards the choir, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.name: Grand Hall
3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.description: The most significant and artistically most important room in the building is the Grand Hall on the second floor, designed after the fire of 1785. Stucco decorations on the walls imitate grey marble with dark veins, while at one time those of the vault were painted light yellow. Architectural decoration powerfully articulates the surfaces.
3d279afa-014f-54de-b5b3-c820b9b5e080.location: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

3f3dd440-a378-5215-abad-afdbb7bd5887.name: Façade of the Asamhaus
3f3dd440-a378-5215-abad-afdbb7bd5887.description: Egid Quirin Asam’s house-turned-atelier is distinguished by its rich, figurative stucco façade. In a sense, it constitutes the secular counterpart to the sacred theme of the church façade. Its content centres on the journey of an artist’s soul in the home of the Muses on Mount Parnassus, with Athena Pallas as its guide.
3f3dd440-a378-5215-abad-afdbb7bd5887.location: To the left of the church

4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.name: Altar and choir
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.description: The choir, oriented to the west, was renewed in 1730 in the contemporary Rococo style. On the occasion of the centennial of the Peace of 1648 a new gallery for the organ was installed. The slightly curved stucco is captivating in its simple elegance, its colour highlighting the choir. Although the gallery continues in the choir, the coloured Regency and Rococo stucco establishes a discrete, almost scenographic quality. The fresco on the ceiling shows the three theological virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity. Around the altar, as at the pulpit, paintings depict scenes from the Life of Christ: the Baptism, Resurrection, Pentecost and Last Supper. The two most important ritualistic elements in the church – altar and pulpit – together harmonise in form and content, dedicated fully to the teachings of Christ.
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.dates: c. 1653: retable; 1673/74: paintings; 1730: organ and decoration of the vault; 1748: renovation of the gallery and organ; 1767: altar
4017c5f2-8879-55a2-83f3-1a52477c3b70.artist: Johann Heiss (1640–1704), Johann Ulrich Mayr (1630–1704), Johannes Spillenberger (1628–1679), Josef Werner (1637–1710); Johann Georg Bergmüller (1688–1762); Johann Esaias Nilson (active 1721–1728); Ignaz Wilhelm Verhelst (1729–1792)

43735349-37aa-5e8a-a34a-c8f426840f79.name: The Life and Veneration of St. John of Nepomuk
43735349-37aa-5e8a-a34a-c8f426840f79.description: The ceiling fresco spans the entire length of the church and is located behind an indirectly lit ledge which appears to be an opening in the ceiling vault. This creates the illusion that one is peering into the eternal heavenly realms. Around the periphery of the vault is a fresco depicting scenes from the life of St. John of Nepomuk and his subsequent veneration.

4692d873-94e6-59eb-9dc0-1830c1081690.name: Ceiling fresco
4692d873-94e6-59eb-9dc0-1830c1081690.description: Guglielmi’s high-grade ceiling fresco depicts allegories of the Four Continents but doesn’t leave any doubt about the supremacy of Europe. Again, the topic shows a clear connection to the life and work of the patron. In the centre of the painting stands Mercury, the god of trade, with a cornucopia. The theme is trade and its worldwide power spreading European comforts, announced by Fame, all over the world. The accentuated exotic design of the figures corresponds with the painted over-doors in the ballroom.

475ce502-c96b-5741-bb58-ee8eb89c4993.name: Plans from the founding charter: Holy sepulchre with “Schlupfwallfahrt”
475ce502-c96b-5741-bb58-ee8eb89c4993.description: The plans from Johann Jakob Herkomer contained in the founding charter envisaged a special feature, a holy sepulchre in the crypt, a so-called “Schlupfwallfahrt”, as built by Herkomer in his own private chapel in Sameister. Access was to be provided by a low passage. Although Herkomer’s ideas found their way into the founding charter they were not realised, possibly on cost grounds, and were replaced by the simpler revised plans from Hafenegger.

48d6ab89-fd69-5029-ab77-89ea887fd268.name: Façade
48d6ab89-fd69-5029-ab77-89ea887fd268.description: The side façade with its five axes and window axes at irregular intervals only has one central polygonal bay window. Horizontally it is concluded by an eaves cornice. The stucco, forming an embellishment around the window openings, has more room to unfold than on the main façade. The architectural forms of the décor, such as the window moulding, are overshadowed by the vigorous outgrowth of ornamentation.

4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.name: Pulpit
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.description: The pulpit, decorated in slender *rocailles*, is positioned prominently within the church *vis-à-vis* the gallery according to its role in the Lutheran rite. A life-size wooden crucifix above the pulpit and two paintings of Christ’s Passion by Johann Heinrich Schönfeld at either side complete the Christological ensemble.
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.location: Wall on the right-hand side, Evangelical Lutheran Church of the Holy Cross
4a57faf0-598d-578a-ae25-67d5b5d35328.artist: Johann Esaias Nilson (1721–1728); Ignaz Wilhelm Verhelst (1729–1792); Johann Heinrich Schönfeld (1609–1684)

4e8a7718-f219-5f1d-baf0-f5d5f51bee94.name: Plague Column
4e8a7718-f219-5f1d-baf0-f5d5f51bee94.description: A plague epidemic struck the town in 1681. Construction of the column began in 1700 opposite the house of the burgher Z. Hodová whose inheritance financed the project. A sculptor from Brtnice was chosen for the job; Brtnice was a renowned centre of arts and crafts. The cloud-like column, surrounded by volute pedestals with statues of the saints, is crowned with the figure of the Virgin Immaculata. The base is furnished by grottos within which are St. Rosalia and Mary Magdalene. The burgher’s legacy inspired other inhabitants to civic generosity and their donations paid for many of the sculptures adorning the town, including the Chapel of the Virgin Mary (1719).

4f5cb1b8-e3a4-57ad-af75-9eeb25ded3f1.name: Hunting scene
4f5cb1b8-e3a4-57ad-af75-9eeb25ded3f1.description: *Azulejos* representing an early 18th-century gallant deer-hunting scene with an elegant lady and gentleman riding what seem to be Lusitano horses. This panel is one of a set of gallant hunting scenes that decorate the entrance room on the first floor. Note that the frame, with typical Baroque architectural and decorative elements, is a tapestry.
4f5cb1b8-e3a4-57ad-af75-9eeb25ded3f1.artist: Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]

50970b92-85d1-59d1-b583-3cd3eb00cd42.name: Detail of the Fortress
50970b92-85d1-59d1-b583-3cd3eb00cd42.location: Built of clay, brick, wood and some stone, the fortress complex was designed to accommodate 4,000 soldiers and 150 cannons.

528f12d4-5b9e-5f75-a717-5d6b25977d21.name: Pagan gods
528f12d4-5b9e-5f75-a717-5d6b25977d21.description: Although these are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

5d2048c3-7fc9-5226-968c-556eab5c57e0.name: Archangel Gabriel
5d2048c3-7fc9-5226-968c-556eab5c57e0.description:
The figure of the Angel of the Annunciation closes a series of statues lining the route from Telč to Staré Město where the Chapel of the Virgin Mary can be seen with decoration by J. L. Daisinger, an assistant of P. Troger.  
K. Ober’s work is seen chiefly in Jaroměřice nad Rokytnou. In Telč he is also responsible for the sculpted decoration on the frontages of two houses in the main square.

5da28193-df85-5125-983e-01722d0be0e4.name: *The fall of Phaeton*
5da28193-df85-5125-983e-01722d0be0e4.description: Burrini is considered the most “baroque” Bolognese painter for his dynamic and fluid painting style. He represents the myth of Phaeton, who is falling down from the sky with his chariot and horses in a sort of vortex.

5da360c8-1992-5262-82c8-43e5fdfbccd1.name: Ground-floor Windows
5da360c8-1992-5262-82c8-43e5fdfbccd1.artist: Architect: André Soares (1720–1769), possibly in association with the decorative artist, Bartolomeu Antunes (1688–1753)

6174afaa-9d22-5990-a88e-438c271eaecb.name: Trophy
6174afaa-9d22-5990-a88e-438c271eaecb.description: Four magnificent stucco trophies decorate the corners of the ballroom ceiling. They represent a unicorn head surrounded with arms and flags, creating an elegant composition.

638b8d0b-c143-5fcb-b7eb-99c572ca9cf5.name: Cartouche with inscription
638b8d0b-c143-5fcb-b7eb-99c572ca9cf5.location: Central part of the arch below the niche

65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.name: Ceiling fresco: *The Veneration of St. Charles Borromeo*
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.description: The frescos in Volders are among the most important of Knoller’s works. The apotheosis of the church patron in the main cupola is the high point of the programme, surrounded by scenes from his life. As an important representative of the Counter Reformation his veneration goes hand in hand with the victory of Catholicism. Knoller’s clear composition with monumental figures already contains elements of Classicism.
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.location: Main cupola, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

65eba8ae-f9a2-5fc2-94ef-563d44d65d3f.name: *Azulejos* depicting the 14 Acts of Mercy
65eba8ae-f9a2-5fc2-94ef-563d44d65d3f.description: *Azulejos* representing the 14 Acts of Mercy cover the walls of the nave. On the Gospel side are the Spiritual Works and on the Epistle side the Corporal. In the central arch, a large *azulejos* panel depicts Our Lady of Mercy, who with her open veil, appears as if protecting the visitors.
65eba8ae-f9a2-5fc2-94ef-563d44d65d3f.artist: Attributed to António and Policarpo de Oliveira Bernardes [n.d.]

663341fb-1727-5934-b72b-3a793d3acfc9.name: The Glory of St. John of Nepomuk
663341fb-1727-5934-b72b-3a793d3acfc9.description: This aedicula façade, inspired by Roman Baroque architecture, appears like a triumphant, altar-like monument in honour of Saint John of Nepomuk. His admission into Heaven, symbolized by the canopy over the entrance adorned with gilded stars, is depicted in the medium of a three-dimensional stone sculpture supported compositionally and iconographically by the building’s architectural motifs.
663341fb-1727-5934-b72b-3a793d3acfc9.artist: Architecture: Cosmas Damian (1686–1739) and Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750) Stucco and Sculpture: Egid Quirin Asam

6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.name: Façade
6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.description: The entire idiosyncrasy and fancy of the Early Baroque building can be best seen on the façade which appears as if it was pieced together from a construction kit composed of the most bizarre forms. The departure from the classical theory of form shows that the dilettante architect (= enthusiast) was still an adherent of Mannerism, drawing his vocabulary of forms from religious tracts. Little of the often classical austerity of German Early Baroque is in evidence here. The chapels at the sides of the façade were added later in accordance with the existing design.

718b140c-3c37-56e7-9342-578e4be4a043.name: Main façade
718b140c-3c37-56e7-9342-578e4be4a043.description: Four storeys, each with three window axes, extend above two compact Late Gothic access arches, with the central axis symmetrically framed by two polygonal bay windows. The building is crowned by a Baroque valley roof gable with volutes and a vertical oval window in the centre. The bold stucco composed of garlands of flowers and fruit, festoons, shells and putti, linked by foliage and strapwork, establish an unusually sculptural accent, thus giving expression to the wealth and prestige of the building’s owner.

73405eca-5c23-5cd2-a06a-559a0200f6cd.name: The Observatory
73405eca-5c23-5cd2-a06a-559a0200f6cd.description: According to Anna Maria Matteucci, when Carlo Francesco Dotti was appointed to the Institute – where he also designed the Library – he modified the plan of his predecessor, Giuseppe Antonio Torri. In particular, consistent with his architectural style, he simplified the baroque motifs giving the tower a severe, neo medieval look.
73405eca-5c23-5cd2-a06a-559a0200f6cd.artist: Giuseppe Antonio Torri; Carlo Francesco Dotti

746b9a00-54e3-5a9c-ad36-ed683d252746.name: Main Door and Bay Window
746b9a00-54e3-5a9c-ad36-ed683d252746.description: Central axis of the building decorated with *Rocaille* motifs.
746b9a00-54e3-5a9c-ad36-ed683d252746.artist: Architect André Soares (1720–1769), possibly in association with the decorative artist, Bartolomeu Antunes (1688–1753)

75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.name: The Holy Trinity
75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.description: The topmost sculpture of Christ the Saviour and God the Father, the ruler of the world, opens with the Archangel Michael, symbol of the eternal struggle against heresy. The dove of the Holy Spirit on a sunburst has its eminence underlined by the rays of the rising sun. Even the Augsburg masters took an interest in the gilding of the copper statues.
75199fa6-69bb-5d9b-b18f-1369a12f7cc8.artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc), Jan Šimon Forstner (1714? Salzburg – 1773 Olomouc)

767b259b-ec09-5677-98c7-f929983f4b2b.name: Drawing of  Pombaline Façades
767b259b-ec09-5677-98c7-f929983f4b2b.description:
Fire became a major concern after the earthquake of 1755 when tightly packed downtown Lisbon was consumed by fire that swept through the narrow streets and quickly destroyed buildings that were built closely together.  
Henceforth, buildings were separated by stone walls in order to isolate them. The uniform, multi-storey Pombaline façades (with shops, three domestic floors and an attic) are unique, constructed at a time when the focus was on safety and cost was a priority.  
The uniformity of the façades and windows is linked to the cost controls that dictated reconstruction: installation of the doors and windows were straightforward once all the stone frames had been made with identical measurements. The addition of a coat of arms was not allowed.

773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.name: *Allegorical celebration of the thermal water in Porretta*
773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.description: This painted decoration was created to celebrate the family by enhancing the therapeutic properties of the thermal water which springs in Porretta, a small village on the mountains around Bologna, a feud of the Ranuzzi from 1482. Girolamo Ranuzzi asked the poet Pier Jacopo Martello to create an iconographic programme to translate in painting. Vittorio Bigari and Stefano Orlandi painted the ceiling between 1724 and 1725.
773672e7-c81d-5cd0-bedd-93bea7b36705.location: Ceiling decoration of the so-called ‘Galleria’, Palazzo Ranuzzi

77da7614-9b91-52f9-a8f6-51683004bb06.name: Panelled ceiling
77da7614-9b91-52f9-a8f6-51683004bb06.description: Presumably the work of master craftsmen schooled in secular architecture, the nave features a wooden panelled ceiling composed of rectangular and octagonal panels and gilded rosettes. Due to the intricacy and interlacing of the panels it was never intended for a programme of pictures. Nevertheless, it lends the space the character of a festive hall and heightens the impression generated by the altars.

798b4fa0-3381-5e10-8b2c-ebe673128ec2.name: Mercury Fountain
798b4fa0-3381-5e10-8b2c-ebe673128ec2.description: Mercury, the Roman god of trade, blesses the town's prosperity at the intersection of two streets. He is depicted with three basic attributes symbolising his vocation: he is wearing a *petasus* (hat to keep off the rain), in his raised right hand he holds a caduceus (a sceptre with a pair of intertwined serpents; a messenger's emblem), and has *talaria* on his feet (winged sandals to enable speedy travel). Mercury was equivalent to the Greek god Hermes, guide to the souls of the dead. The fountain thus features three serpentine dolphin gargoyles, symbolising three underworld rivers, the Lethe, the Styx and the Acheron.
798b4fa0-3381-5e10-8b2c-ebe673128ec2.artist: Václav Render (1669–1733 Olomouc), Filip Sattler (1695 Wenns, Tyrol – 1738 Olomouc)

79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.name: Vault of the Grand Hall
79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.description: The vault is divided into four sections by diagonal strips. In between each section, there are round medallions with scenes from Roman military history, as well as emblems with the motifs of antique military equipment: shields, torches and flags.
79ee1d89-b25b-54b7-9f77-22260ee5d520.location: Second floor, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

7e5a4283-522d-5505-981d-d1cf2b78769d.name: Slope and Ditch with Bulwark and Ravelin
7e5a4283-522d-5505-981d-d1cf2b78769d.description: Besides its military efficiency, the large earthworks and buildings were important to social cohesion. The bulk of the architecture was a rhetorical statement that the country could face any menace from foreign armies. The fortification was, therefore built both symbolically and practically to discourage further enemy actions.

7fe4d5db-8af3-5754-8d9b-bd7179d3b9bd.name: Egypt
7fe4d5db-8af3-5754-8d9b-bd7179d3b9bd.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656, Graz – 1723, Vienna), Anton Riga (around 1660, Královec – 1728, Brno)

811c78b3-34d9-54df-bc61-6623d14d26f2.name: Pulpit
811c78b3-34d9-54df-bc61-6623d14d26f2.description: The pulpit from the sculptor Moll from Innsbruck is an especially opulent example of a Baroque pulpit. The richly curved forms of the foot, parapet and baldachin feature a wealth of figures and symbols, including personifications of the divine virtues at the foot of the cupola and evangelist symbols on the baldachin.

83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.name: Three out of the six original plans with a new layout sympathetic to the old one; final plan and orthophoto of Lisbon
83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.description: Following the earthquake of 1755, the Marquis of Pombal rapidly ordered a competition for the design of *Baixa Pombalina*. Six plans were submitted from which he would select the winner. On 4 December 1755, Manuel da Maia and Eugénio dos Santos presented plans that proposed replacing Terreiro do Paço (Palace Square) with Praça do Comércio, conceived as a monumental entrance into the town through the Cais das Colunas (Columns Quay).
83a35999-406e-5ef3-a9b6-1e038d1d60e2.artist: Military engineers: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760)

83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.name: Right hand-side altar
83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.description: The artistic highlight of the ensemble is the right hand-side altar from unpainted Swiss pine wood, probably the work of the carver Michael Lechleitner from Grins. The altar, which according to the inscription was donated by Susanne Kolp and Elisabeth Linser in 1652, is one of the most important German Early Baroque altars. In continuation of Late Gothic traditions it is covered in rich ornamental carvings from the repertoire of the Late Renaissance, while the overall form – a column aedicule raised on a high plinth with a vertical oval altar crown – is already characterised by Baroque forms.
83d3decd-9c3a-5aca-8af7-4d9325db876f.location: Southeast nave on the triumphal arch wall

84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.name: *Gaiolas* Building Structure
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.description: *The Gaiola Pombalina* is a remarkable symmetrical structure built from wood to distribute and balance the forces of an earthquake. All buildings in downtown Lisbon were built according to this system, and this is the world's first anti-seismic structure. This prototype, built by the fire department at the beginning of the 20th century, is used for fire-fighting training.
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.location: *Baixa Pombalina* or downtown Lisbon. These drawings are displayed in Museu da Cidade and a prototype is in the Museu dos Bombeiros.
84149fe6-4a0e-5c7e-942e-8173633f866e.artist: Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763), Manuel da Maia (1677–1766)

8514c9c2-742c-59b9-b32a-26fca7a59c83.name: Main entrance
8514c9c2-742c-59b9-b32a-26fca7a59c83.description: The presence of two imposing figures (telamones) supporting the balcony of the first floor characterises the portal of the palace. Work of Gabrielle Brunelli and Francesco Agnesini, the telamones are made of local but very friable sandstone, called ‘macigno’. Thanks to the telamones the building is also known as the ‘palace of the giants.’ (il palazzo dei giganti).

85d4ddf7-7782-5fd0-9f12-244d2aa92c0b.name: Jesuit College and the Church of the Name of Jesus
85d4ddf7-7782-5fd0-9f12-244d2aa92c0b.description: The construction of both college and church are associated with the Counter-Reformation and the active approach of the Jesuits after the Battle of White Mountain in 1620. The management of the Jesuit College in Jindřichův Hradec made the best of their influence with the owner of the demesne and, after purchasing several houses in the town, they established a seat of the order there. In the west section of the square the original narrow frontages of burgher houses were broken by a monumental two-floor construction and with a church in a new style, styles which influenced all further building in Telč. The church was decorated by various European artists: V. Kovanda, F. J. Hamb, K. Škréta, J.  J. Heinsch, D. Gran and I. Raab.

873719b6-be77-587a-8bfa-0e77decf061d.name: Plan of Slavonski Brod Fortress
873719b6-be77-587a-8bfa-0e77decf061d.description:
A regular star-shaped fortress (1691-1731) with the church of St. Anne (1743)  
in the middle. Placed at the centre of the Fortress, the pavilion style church was designed to stand over an independent tabernacle-altar situated at its centre.

8817f196-3685-51fa-b249-38607df00ba9.name: Northern side façade
8817f196-3685-51fa-b249-38607df00ba9.description: Religious motifs are no longer to be found on the side façades instead they are completely devoted to the amusement of the viewer. While the south side features a false window with a woman looking out, the north side is largely decorated with exotic animals in accordance with the fashion of the time. Three monkeys are sitting on the cornice with a basket of fruit, above them a parrot on a stick and a cat at the other end of the cornice.

89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.name: Monumental staircase
89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.description:
Around 1688 Annibale Ranuzzi commissioned the construction of a monumental staircase for his residential palace in Bologna. The presence of a monumental staircase was a very important element in the baroque ceremonies connected with Bolognese senatorial class political and social activities.  
It is not possible to identify the creator of the staircase. Some believe he must be identified with Giovanni Battista Torri, who paid for the wood model of the work. Others believe he must be identified with the famous Carlo Fontana, who was contacted by the patron together with other architects.  
The work was finished around 1695.
89542836-1bd2-508a-9e55-b7f2185eb881.artist: Giovanni Battista Torri (?), Carlo Fontana (?), Ercole Graziani; Filippo Balugani

8c5e9db1-f7d8-5032-8c56-6187b6c635db.name: Neptune Fountain
8c5e9db1-f7d8-5032-8c56-6187b6c635db.description: The oldest of the series of Olomouc fountains is dedicated to the water god, believed to protect the town from the watery elements. Its counterpart is the Jupiter Fountain (1707), invoking the ruler of the heavenly pantheon.

8ce96854-8c7d-59a9-952c-b295df7f550a.name: *Glorification of the Miti family*
8ce96854-8c7d-59a9-952c-b295df7f550a.description: the ceiling is decorated with a motive of niches with cartouches and corbels; in the middle is represented an allegorical scene.
8ce96854-8c7d-59a9-952c-b295df7f550a.location: Palazzo Miti Zagnoni, first floor, hall of honour, ceiling

916476d2-c19c-58a3-8bc7-4dbd353724d6.name: Parnassus Fountain
916476d2-c19c-58a3-8bc7-4dbd353724d6.description: “Art monuments” have their clients and designers as well as those who build them, the stonemasons, builders and other craftsmen, and sometimes bureaucrats as well. The construction of the fountain was administered by the Senator of Brno, J. I. Dechau. He supervised the architect and managed the builders and, when it was completed, he had a print engraved in which he proudly stated his name under the picture. He may be the man depicted here explaining the fountain’s symbolism to a group of aristocrats.

965899fc-aa3e-5147-ae6e-550eff2b95c8.name: Loggia and arcades
965899fc-aa3e-5147-ae6e-550eff2b95c8.description: A scenographic view of the loggia shows different points of view obtained through the use of columns, balustrades and arcades. This is typical of the local baroque tradition.

9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.name: View from the east
9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.description: Although the arrangement of the rest of the building is not as closely crowded as the façade, the walls are still un-classical in their configuration. The superstructure with perimeter pilasters throughout and an attic zone is modelled on St. Peter’s in Rome, as is the building’s basic design with domed tri-conch. The tower, expressing the motif of the Trinity, was originally designed with a spiral-shaped pinnacle.

9786138c-911e-5c83-bbbc-1f79f78efc26.name: Patio with stairs to the first floor
9786138c-911e-5c83-bbbc-1f79f78efc26.description: The patio, with stairs to the first floor, creates a refined entrance space decorated with figurative *azulejos*: a welcoming figure stands at the top of the staircase, which throughout its course is decorated with designs of architectural balusters, *putti* and vases of flowers.
9786138c-911e-5c83-bbbc-1f79f78efc26.location: Entrance to the building, House of the Holy Body (Museum of Baroque)
9786138c-911e-5c83-bbbc-1f79f78efc26.artist: Architect unknown. Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]

97fcd65c-140e-5f02-af6d-be912af1408c.name: *Glorification of the Miti family*
97fcd65c-140e-5f02-af6d-be912af1408c.description: Justice holds the scale while Right lays a lily on it.
97fcd65c-140e-5f02-af6d-be912af1408c.location: Palazzo Miti Zagnoni, first floor, hall of honour, ceiling

9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.name: High altar and miraculous picture
9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.description: The high altar is one of the most important examples of the Baroque staging of an older sacred picture. The miraculous picture *Mariahilf* from Lucas Cranach was originally housed in Dresden and found its way to Innsbruck as a gift to Archduke Leopold V. It has been on display in the parish church since 1650. It became the most widespread picture of the Virgin Mary in the alpine region. It was integrated into the high altar, built in 1726, as a “picture within a picture” (with exchangeable frames, which during Lent displays a picture from Josef Schöpf, at all other times a silver frame). The high altar is flanked by statues of the patron saints of the Diocese of Brixen, Ingenuin and Albuin.
9927d984-2b47-57ca-b768-827d5abf75c0.artist: Lucas Cranach the Elder (1472–1553); Cristoforo Benedetti (1660–1735), Theodor Benedetti [n.d.]; Josef Schöpf (1745–1822)

9ae9fc2b-3bed-5ffe-b81b-cb6a18a7f879.name: “Noble” or first-floor windows
9ae9fc2b-3bed-5ffe-b81b-cb6a18a7f879.artist: Architect: André Soares (1720–1769), possibly in association with the decorative artist, Bartolomeu Antunes (1688–1753)

9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.name: Imaginary cityscape in the Salon with Panoramic Views
9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.description: The wall paintings of imaginary cityscapes reveal the influence of the architectural drawings of Giovanni Battista Piranesi.
9dddcf81-e7ef-57de-826f-00c891445be3.location: Second floor, west salon, Palace of the Sugar Refinery

9df17b0c-56ba-5fdc-8d9a-c7177fbc1afc.name: Casemates for the Military
9df17b0c-56ba-5fdc-8d9a-c7177fbc1afc.description: A row of buildings to accommodate military casemates. Eighteen of the twenty underground rooms have ventilation, access to a well, a water mine and a water-drainage system. In case of attack, the townspeople would seek refuge in the underground rooms, which also served as military lodgings, a warehouse and even as hospital in critical periods.
9df17b0c-56ba-5fdc-8d9a-c7177fbc1afc.artist: Pierre Gilles de Saint-Paul,Manuel de Azevedo Fortes  and others

a0121cc0-20a3-5469-8da2-4993a1e95a3a.name: Main façade
a0121cc0-20a3-5469-8da2-4993a1e95a3a.description: The end side facing the Untermarkt is the magnificently decorated main façade of the house with a central bay window. Architecture paintings form the structure and frame for the images. At the bay window the central motifs are presented, in the middle below the window the Mary Help picture from Innsbruck carried by putti, above it God the Father and the Holy Ghost. On the side walls further putti are depicted playing with a wind wheel and bird cage, while the putti to the side of the bay window present the Tablets of the Law with the Ten Commandments, the Cross of Christ and a chalice. The gable zone features a peacock. The overall appearance is primarily a result of the virtuoso rocaille frames around the windows. Cornice and gable, both painted, form the upper termination.

a3be46cc-799f-5f24-bbf9-715af2876ed1.name: High altar
a3be46cc-799f-5f24-bbf9-715af2876ed1.description: The high altar, possibly a work of Johann Georg Pauer from Tannheim, was built around 1710. Its massive, completely gilded superstructure with projecting strutted pediment above spiral columns is one of the most important achievements of High Baroque altar-construction in Außerfern. The altarpiece from the Baroque painter Johannes Heel from Pfronten in Allgäu depicting the Adoration of the Shepherds is situated beneath the ceiling fresco of the *Adoration of the Holy Trinity*.
a3be46cc-799f-5f24-bbf9-715af2876ed1.location: Choir, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

a567bfc0-3ec2-5307-8a47-ec8ecae7cc75.name: Hercules
a567bfc0-3ec2-5307-8a47-ec8ecae7cc75.description: Hercules, symbol of strength and courage, holds Cerberus, the guardian of the underworld, in chains.
a567bfc0-3ec2-5307-8a47-ec8ecae7cc75.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656, Graz – 1723, Vienna), Tobias Kracker (1658, Vienna – 1736, Vienna)

a93a44e4-31d3-5087-ab94-f1ff9655efb5.name: Balustrade
a93a44e4-31d3-5087-ab94-f1ff9655efb5.artist: Architect: André Soares (1720–1769), possibly in association with the decorative artist, Bartolomeu Antunes (1688–1753)

a9e8aaa6-04ad-5a03-89b4-55c42fe97bbd.name: Burgher House No. 59/I
a9e8aaa6-04ad-5a03-89b4-55c42fe97bbd.description: The frontages of almost 50 per cent of the houses were re-plastered in the first quarter of the 18th century, not purely for decorative reasons but also because the requirements placed on housing had changed. New larger windows made the interiors considerably lighter. The houses began to feature elements of the Radical Baroque, lacking completely the basic architecture of Telc, and generally rather scarce in Moravia in contrast to Bohemia. The undulating effect of the frontages is enhanced by diagonally positioned pilasters reaching up to the gable tops that are crowned with a window and a vase.

add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.name: Praça do Comércio
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.description: Praça do Comércio overlooking the River Tejo is an emblematic part of the *Baixa*. According to the engraving attributed to Gaspar Froes Machado, the initial plans were not entirely fulfilled; the triumphal arch was finally built in 1873 according to the design of Veríssimo José da Costa.
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.location: Facing the estuary of the River Tagus
add54831-b132-5b1c-9ed1-5c4eec59a759.artist: Initial plans of Praça do Comércio: Manuel da Maia (1677–1766), Eugénio dos Santos (1711–1760); Carlos Mardel (c. 1695–1763); triumphal arch: Veríssimo José da Costa [n.d.] assisted by Vítor Bastos (1830–1894) and Anatole C. Calmels (1822–1906)

b0b74c0a-ea2d-5127-a642-8a836ff47fcb.name: Loggia
b0b74c0a-ea2d-5127-a642-8a836ff47fcb.description: Central view of the loggia on the front with the so called serliana or Palladian window.

b2980c5d-4b8e-5737-b1bd-ebbf38274aad.name: High altar
b2980c5d-4b8e-5737-b1bd-ebbf38274aad.description: The high altar, which according to an inscription on the predella was built in 1651 as an endowment of the Weinzierl family, is the oldest of the three altars in the Church. It is an aedicula altar with a broken segmental pediment and an openwork altar crown. At the centre of the programme of figures are the church’s three patron saints, all of whom are invoked as protection from the plague.

b478afb3-6caa-520b-bcbb-1a527eca0896.name: St. John the Baptist
b478afb3-6caa-520b-bcbb-1a527eca0896.description: The individual, larger-than-life figures are veiled in light, airy cloaks. Their austere gesticulation and postures correspond with their spiritual facial expressions. The picturesque outlines of the figures enhance the aesthetic impression of a pyramid-like whole. Following Zahner’s death the sculptural decoration was completed by W. Träger and J. M. Scherhauf. They continued with the sculptor’s initial concept and achieved features typical of Zahner in a side-altar figure for the Místek Church.

b48cb5d9-82ce-54c1-ab46-61d861c8e0cc.name: Loggia and arcades
b48cb5d9-82ce-54c1-ab46-61d861c8e0cc.description: A scenographic view of the loggia shows different points of view obtained through the use of columns, balustrades and arcades. This is typical of the local baroque tradition.

b9250751-a918-5753-8ef7-c308b77cd4dd.name: Fountain Design
b9250751-a918-5753-8ef7-c308b77cd4dd.artist: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656, Graz – 1723, Vienna)

bbf2ac31-f420-5547-903d-485e39009fa1.name: Arches over the Alcântara valley
bbf2ac31-f420-5547-903d-485e39009fa1.description: The structure uses the pointed arch in some of the larger arches crossing the Alcântara valley. Curiously, some of the stones of the Aqueduct are inscribed with the masons' initials, a custom that was all but lost but which was revived here.

bf66d04d-bf53-5799-aa15-41c2f4772599.name: Caesar Fountain
bf66d04d-bf53-5799-aa15-41c2f4772599.description: The rearing horse with rider stands on a rock; at the horse’s feet lie two figures of bearded men, water deities, representing the rivers Morava and Danube. Their joined hands and forward movement indicate the confluence of the two rivers. The men hold the emblems of Moravia and Lower Austria, symbolising the alliance of the two countries and their joint future in loyalty (personified by a resting dog) to the emperor.
bf66d04d-bf53-5799-aa15-41c2f4772599.artist: Jan Jiří Schauberger (?, before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.name: Middle room balcony railings
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.description: Each room has a different colour scheme and decorative emphasis with multicoloured bookshelves of different lacquered finishes in green, red and black decorated with *chinoiserie* motifs. Each of the rooms is two-storeys high, with a balcony and stairs incorporated into the furniture.
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.artist: Design and execution: Francesco Gualdini, João Rodrigues de Almeida; supervisor: Gaspar Ferreira; painting and gilding of woodwork: Manuel da Silva [dates unknown]

c6e385c3-ce5d-59a2-9749-9c9b67369cb0.name: St. Cyril
c6e385c3-ce5d-59a2-9749-9c9b67369cb0.description: The six statues on the central section represent Slavic saints: Methodius, the first Moravian bishop; Cyril (Konstantin); Vojtěch the Bishop of Prague and founder of the first Benedictine Monastery in Bohemia; John of Nepomuk; John Sarkander, tortured to death in Olomouc in 1620; and St. Blasius to whom the Olomouc Church, considered the oldest Baroque church in the country, was dedicated.

c8223071-8449-5de7-8edc-1087729762f4.name: Tile-Painting Masters’ signature, P.M.P.
c8223071-8449-5de7-8edc-1087729762f4.description: The signature P.M.P is probably that of Padre Manuel Pereira, who was a clergyman, amateur architect (in the 18th century he designed the palace of the Tristão da Cunha family) and *azulejos* painter. Padre Manuel Pereira was patron of a large workshop in Lisbon. He had several disciples that produced *azulejos* for palaces and churches all over Portugal and Brazil.
c8223071-8449-5de7-8edc-1087729762f4.artist: Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]

c8702876-ac37-5902-bf15-743a186cb380.name: Gates of St Anthony (Santo António) - exterior and interior
c8702876-ac37-5902-bf15-743a186cb380.description: Gates designed in the Classical style of French military architecture.

ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.name: Left hand-side altar
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.description: The left hand-side altar built after 1682 differs fundamentally from the other altars. Its superstructure forms a frame for the two inset paintings; the larger of the two, the actual altarpiece, is the work of Michael Waldmann from 1677 and depicts St. Anthony in front of the Infant Jesus with the portrait of the picture’s donor, the musician Karl Boussier from Innsbruck. The picture was brought to Landeck in 1682. Each side of the altar’s outer frame forms seven small niches with figures of the fourteen Holy Helpers, probably the work of Adam Payr.
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.location: Northeast nave on the triumphal arch wall
ca4be14d-93e9-596d-b076-3472190bbd99.artist: Adam Payr (?–1682); Michael Waldmann the younger (1640–1682)

cb4fde26-f723-5c3f-926c-8f4ec43eb1b2.name: Crucifix
cb4fde26-f723-5c3f-926c-8f4ec43eb1b2.description: A further special feature of the interior work is the so-called “Wundheiland” or “Tropfheiland”, an expressive “plague cross” suspended from the apex of the triumphal arch. The body is covered in wounds from which blood flows. The suffering Christ as the symbol of all pain and its overcoming is presented to the itinerant workers as a sign of consolation and warning.
cb4fde26-f723-5c3f-926c-8f4ec43eb1b2.location: Choir arch, Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph

cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.name: Staircase
cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.description: The Imperial-style staircase has three flights. It bears characteristics typical of the 1780s, consisting of superimposed columns, strips and cornices originally painted in a marble paint finish, while the railing has a decorative motif of a square meander, which also points to the Early Classical language of architecture.
cc3d0593-4799-50e0-9f3d-44bc2af39e0e.location: Central area (opposite the entrance hall), Palace of the Sugar Refinery

d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.name:
Bronze Equestrian Statue of King José I  
(copper engraving by Carneiro da Silva made before the unveiling in 1774)
d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.description: The statue by Joaquim Machado de Castro was unveiled on 27 May 1775 on King José I’s birthday. The copper engraving by Joaquim Carneiro da Silva was made a year prior to this in 1774 to commemorate the unveiling. Other commemorative items include china decorated with reproductions of the statue.
d2a0bb6d-e271-5430-bd69-fba3a45eaf85.location: Terreiro do Paço (Palace Square) or Praça do Comércio (Commerce  Square)

d2a7f2b6-6580-5dae-8336-b155d38a911d.name: Interior, facing east
d2a7f2b6-6580-5dae-8336-b155d38a911d.description: The interior of the Burschlkirche is characterised by the contrast between plane architecture, employing an antiquated repertoire of forms, and the masterfully executed, rich ensemble of the three altars. The two-bay choir with a 3/6 termination in the continuation of the Gothic tradition is separated from the nave by a heavily tapered ogival triumphal arch. This in turn is a simple oblong hall which the panelled ceiling lends the character of a secular festive hall of the Renaissance period.

d33bac06-e82c-5db0-b385-be388a6eeb7a.name: Tritons’ Fountain
d33bac06-e82c-5db0-b385-be388a6eeb7a.description: Václav Render, who also created several other fountains and columns, was an Olomouc burgher and stonemason, inspired by Bernini’s fountain in Rome. The Olomouc fountain represents the descendants and servants of Neptune, the ruler of the sea. Triton, half-man half-fish, son of Neptune and Amphitrite, would sound his conch if there was a storm at sea.The fountain may therefore symbolise a warning against the watery elements, far from unjustified in the vicinity of the mighty and unpredictable River Morava. The fountain originally dominated a crossroads.

d554971f-f508-52e4-999c-e09207ee45b2.name: Ceiling of the Galleria del Senato
d554971f-f508-52e4-999c-e09207ee45b2.description: The personification of Bologna is standing on a chariot pulled by two lions, which symbolize the power of the City. She is guided by Cybele, the goddess of nature, to the glory of Olympus, where Jupiter welcomes her.

d6106d67-8053-5953-b8d3-21dcd5e36a0d.name: Mãe d’ Água das Amoreiras reservoir
d6106d67-8053-5953-b8d3-21dcd5e36a0d.description: Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras reservoir was designed by Carlos Mardel. Due to its monumentality, the Mãe d'Água constitutes a true civic temple to the *águas livres* (free waters). An antechamber precedes the vast rectangle which contains a deep reservoir.

d91086bf-1c10-54ef-9ee9-fd787e402072.name: Pagan gods
d91086bf-1c10-54ef-9ee9-fd787e402072.description: Although these are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.name: Light-bearer
d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.description: Light played a major role in Baroque iconography as a symbol of the Holy Spirit and was synonymous with holiness. Angels, the mediators of God's Will, are represented on the bottom balustrade of the staircase as decorative *putti*, messengers and guardians of the light.
d982fe8c-5b31-5e71-98c1-24e9b98b2b9a.artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc) and workshop

d996062b-2320-5362-a028-3354728f180e.name: The Mercy Seat
d996062b-2320-5362-a028-3354728f180e.description: Four winding columns, deliberately imitating the ciborium of St. Peter’s Basilica in Rome, form a pictorial space in front of the upper high altar. There, instead of the modern glory window, a relief of the church’s patron once hung. It is into this space that the Holy Trinity seems to descend in the company of angels. This array of sculptures follows the iconography of the Mercy Seat: God the Father is shown presenting His crucified Son. Moreover, the papal crown that He is wearing, together with the winding columns, symbolizes the Catholic Church’s claim to religious leadership.

de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.name: Monochrome roundel with the *Birth of the Virgin*
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.description: The use of monochrome painting in the roundels at the foot of the dome shows Mitelli’s and Colonna’s elegant taste together with their will to emphasise the contrast between the different worlds of the stories of the Virgin and the heavenly vision above. The scene represented in this roundel is strongly indebted to the classicizing style of Guido Reni.
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.location: Dome of the square antechamber of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
de6db7d5-6d7b-5926-ad6b-637eedb72f0d.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

dfe1817b-f94e-59bb-b55c-9eb4977a08bc.name: View of the west section of Zelný trh (Vegetable Market)
dfe1817b-f94e-59bb-b55c-9eb4977a08bc.description: The upper section of the vegetable market is dominated by the Dietrichstein Palace. This was constructed on the site of five burgher houses by the Olomouc Cardinal, František of Dietrichstein, in 1614–20 and rebuilt in 1739 to 1740 to the designs of G. G. Tencalla. Empress Maria Theresa stayed at No. 9 during her visit to Brno. The empress took part in, among other events, the Procession of Corpus Christi in 1748. The aristocracy and prelates that came to Brno for sessions of the Provincial Assembly constructed and reconstructed a large number of buildings in the city after the Thirty Years’ War, making Brno the third major centre of palace culture in the monarchy after Vienna and Prague.

e782bf6e-5adc-5df3-a2ab-2d9db58b30af.name: Gates of São Francisco (St. Francis) – exterior and interior gates
e782bf6e-5adc-5df3-a2ab-2d9db58b30af.description: Main entrance following the designs of Salomon de Brosse.

e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.name: Playing Putti
e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.description: In the side lunettes of the Room of Fortune are depicted playing putti.
e93c0684-321e-58c9-b7f4-2505ffdc37b6.location: Ceiling decoration of a room of the first floor of the palace, detail, Palazzo Ranuzzi

e9ee182e-3c06-5ca0-afa2-0e2ef8d51fa6.name: Monumental staircase
e9ee182e-3c06-5ca0-afa2-0e2ef8d51fa6.description: Commissioned by Earl Vincenzo Bargellini, the monumental staircase was realised by the architect Alfonso Torreggiani in 1730. The project represents the synthesis resulting from the combination of the designs suggested by various architects contacted by the Earl. Besides Torreggiani, one can see the hints of the work of Carlo Francesco Dotti and Antonio Conti, whose drawings are still preserved. The plastic decorations are the work of Giuseppe Borelli a member of an important Swiss family of stucco decorators, working in Bologna for many noble families. The staircase was recently restored.

eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.name: Carmo Fountain
eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.description: From the Mãe d' Água das Amoreiras reservoir, a secondary aqueduct spreads out around the city terminating in fountains, many of them like this one still extant. Built by the engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco in 1769, it was redesigned by Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos in 1786.
eb7a0351-f4ca-5902-b8bb-572d211a56e6.artist: Attributed to the engineer, Miguel Ângelo Blasco (1769–1770) and the architect, Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos [n.d.]

eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.name: *Choirs of angels with a double crown of flowers and stars*
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.description: Above the extraordinary altar containing the statue of the Virgin Mitelli, and Colonna painted a monumental baroque building, with courts, balconies, friezes and floral decorations. The sky opens over two choirs of angels holding a crown made of flowers, symbolizing earthly grace, and a crown made of stars, a symbol of divine glory. The skilled use of perspective, the vivid colours and the employ of gold leaf in the decorations lead to a strongly visual result.
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.location: Semi dome of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
eb86b19e-ab63-5c13-b4c8-efb32827e0c8.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli

ed6f3189-e588-5b12-a94c-6f71f36b6d21.name: Hercules
ed6f3189-e588-5b12-a94c-6f71f36b6d21.description: Although these figures are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

ee0459a7-7135-59f3-8a2f-96ace2250f9f.name: Ceiling fresco
ee0459a7-7135-59f3-8a2f-96ace2250f9f.description: Already on the staircase, the profession, rank and claim to power of von Liebenhofen are demonstrated. The ceiling is decorated with an oval fresco by Guglielmi, framed within gold-plated stucco. Its theme is the benefices of trade for the arts and sciences.

ef57f78a-4a61-572b-9295-1a1a823103d5.name: Ballroom
ef57f78a-4a61-572b-9295-1a1a823103d5.description: This great hall is considered one of the most peculiar interiors in Italian Baroque architecture. It is a triple volume hall with several balustrades, culminating with the lantern on the top (33 m. height and about 800 square feet surface). There is no painted decoration, only white stucco mouldings that emphasise the extreme lightness of the architecture.

ef5ad0a6-fe89-5362-8d56-f6086ab50208.name: Bulwark
ef5ad0a6-fe89-5362-8d56-f6086ab50208.description: The Bulwark of St. João de Deus for 28 cannons with casemates.
ef5ad0a6-fe89-5362-8d56-f6086ab50208.artist: Pierre Gilles de Saint-Paul and others

ef9ea3ed-fa20-5118-8e8e-67dcd70aa609.name: Caesar
ef9ea3ed-fa20-5118-8e8e-67dcd70aa609.description: The central motif of the fountain is a figure of G. J. Caesar considered, from the 15th century onwards as the founder of the city. The sculptor J. J. Schauberger, chiefly active in Olomouc and Brno, created his masterpieces, this equestrian statue, which was possibly inspired by Bernini's *Constantine the Great* in the Vatican. Caesar's dynasty was allegedly linked to the mythical Hercules. Together with a fountain dedicated to Hercules (1688), the statue celebrates a legend of the establishment of the town. Hercules holds a shield bearing an eagle, symbol of Olomouc, in his left hand.
ef9ea3ed-fa20-5118-8e8e-67dcd70aa609.artist: Jan Jiří Schauberger (?, before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)

f4cd8092-6856-50bc-98ac-2704192e2c1c.name: Staircase
f4cd8092-6856-50bc-98ac-2704192e2c1c.description: View of one of the two stair flights that bring to the loggia.
f4cd8092-6856-50bc-98ac-2704192e2c1c.location: Ground floor, on the front of the villa

fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.name: Detail of ceiling painting
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.description: The *Trompe l'oeil* ceiling painting depicts three manifestations of Wisdom: an allegory of the library (*Bibliotheca*), of the university (*Universitas*) and of the encyclopaedia (*Encyclopaedia*).
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.artist: António Simões Ribeiro and Vicente Nunes [n.d.]

fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.name: Portrait of João V
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.description: The portrait of the King João V emerges from a sort of a “*rideau de scène*” in carved wood, upheld by angels. The oil on canvas painting is by Domenico Duprà, royal painter in Lisbon before 1730.
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

fba45a53-75fe-54df-af59-5265c31ccabf.name: Church Vault with scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary and Jesus.
fba45a53-75fe-54df-af59-5265c31ccabf.description: *Azulejos* decorate the chancel with scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary and Jesus, signed by Policarpo de Oliveira Bernardes.
